Characteristics of Life
5.Living things can reproduce–Life onlydevelops from life–Therefore, living things must be able to create new organisms, and pass on genetic material, or genes–Unicellular splitting or division–Asexual–Identical to parent–Union of sperm and egg–Sexual–Combination of parents
explanation: This slide details the fifth characteristic of life: living things can reproduce. Under the principle that life only develops from life, organisms must create new organisms and pass on genetic material (genes). Reproduction can be asexual, such as unicellular splitting or division, which results in offspring identical to the parent. Alternatively, it can be sexual, involving the union of sperm and egg, which results in a combination of traits from both parents.

questions.q: Which type of reproduction results in offspring that are genetically identical to the parent?
questions.exp: The text defines 'Asexual' reproduction (e.g. unicellular splitting or division) as resulting in offspring that are 'Identical to parent'.
